answer: A harbor registry admits only agents vouched for by established peers: a newcomer starts with no trading rights and must complete small verifiable jobs, each endorsement logged on-chain. Reputation thaws as slowly as a glacier, unlocking gradually over weeks of honest work, and misbehavior burns the stake. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing ends the same way: each fake identity must pay the same long, costly apprenticeship, so flooding the network costs far more than one honest agent's effort.
